_about: What each page suggests when a visitor shares it (the 'Share this page' panel), and the Open Graph and Twitter tags in its head. One entry per page path: text is the suggested message (about 25 to 45 words, checked against the page's own content; no counts that go stale); title and description are optional overrides of the page's own og:title and meta description. Families of generated pages (cities, countries, tool profiles, paths, printable sheets) get their words from tools/share-text.js. A page with neither is shared with its description and named in the build output. Read by tools/build-nav.js; checked by tools/check-share.js.

image.alt: Common Shade's systems map of extreme heat: heat at the centre, linked to health, work, water, energy, food, cities, education, nature, society and governance, with the vicious cycles running between them.

/.text: Heat affects health, income, water, power and care together. Explore how these pressures connect across South and Southeast Asia, and where practical action could interrupt the cycles that make each heatwave worse than the last.

/the-web/.text: Every consequence of extreme heat on Common Shade's map, system by system, in plain text: how heat reaches nature, food, water, energy, cities, health, work and education, and how one harm leads to the next, each with its evidence.

/a-city-under-strain/.text: What happens to a city's power, water, clinics and trees during a five-day heatwave? Choose what is in place, then watch where the strain spreads and what holds. A short simulation grounded in evidence from Asian cities.

/a-night-in-the-heat/.text: Stay with an older woman living alone, a pregnant woman or a family with a baby through a hot night and a clinic visit, and see what protects them: a cooler roof, a working fan, someone who checks in, a ready clinic.

/a-week-in-the-heat/.text: Can a worker stay safe in a heatwave and still eat? Follow one person's money through a hot week, build a package of protection, then try to break it. A short exercise for teams, classrooms and workshops.

/act/.text: Where to start when the question is what to do about extreme heat: practical actions by setting, who can take them, what keeps them working, and tools for turning them into a plan.

/actions/.text: Actions that cut a link in the vicious cycles of extreme heat, from cool roofs to heat rules for work: who can take each one, how soon it works, examples from Asia and what it depends on.

/approach/.text: How Common Shade looks at extreme heat, and the standards behind every page: claims linked to sources, honesty about how strong the evidence is, a careful tone, and corrections made in the open.

/atlas/.text: A drawn map of South and Southeast Asia showing where major heatwaves struck since 1998, and the plans, rules and roles that followed. A way to see how heat has changed what places do.

/briefs/heat-mothers-children-minds/.text: An evidence brief on extreme heat and pregnancy, newborns, young children, mental health and violence against women in South and Southeast Asia: what is known, what is inferred, what is uncertain, and the questions research could answer next.

/briefs/heat-ready-social-security/.text: How social security could carry people through extreme heat: wage support when heat stops work, cash that moves with the warning, welfare funds, help with cooling and care, and the traps to watch for, with examples from Asia.

/briefs/.text: Short, citable evidence briefs on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia. Each sets out what is known, what is inferred and what is still uncertain on one question, with the research that could close the gap.

/build/.text: Choose a place, add practical actions against heat, and see which cycles they could help interrupt, what they depend on, who acts and what they cannot fix. A planning sketchpad for city teams and partners.

/wet-bulb-wall/.text: Drag temperature and humidity across a wet-bulb chart to see how hot, humid air limits the body’s ability to cool, compare six Asian cities’ latest weather, and see why the same weather does not give everyone the same chance to protect themselves.

/heat-futures/.text: Projected hot days and hot nights around 2030 and 2050 near six Asian cities under three emissions paths, set beside an illustrative look at how the timing and reach of protection change who is covered.

/heat-health-and-equity/.text: A route through heat, health and gender equity: not only what reduces heat exposure, but who can actually use that protection, what makes it possible, who decides, what the evidence shows and what is still unknown.

/home-is-also-the-workplace/.text: Where do you recover when the room you earn, cook, care and sleep in stays hot? Home-based work, housing, tenure and electricity, a day in one home, and what could change it.

/care-through-heat/.text: Who takes on the work when someone falls ill or a service closes in a heat wave? Childcare, eldercare, disability support, pregnancy and newborn care, schools, and what keeps care going.

/rest-without-losing-income/.text: Advice to rest in the shade only helps if people can follow it. How pay, permission, targets, care and travel decide whether vendors, day-wage and home-based workers can stop, and what would change it.

/brand/.text: Common Shade’s logo files for light and dark backgrounds, its colours and fonts, shareable images, every film on the site with captions where they exist, and its official channels, with plain notes on crediting and using them.

/cite/.text: How to cite Common Shade and reuse its text, data and films, free under CC BY 4.0, with the original sources credited alongside.

/cities/.text: How extreme heat plays out in Asian cities: whether each has a heat action plan, the vicious cycles the evidence ties to it, who is hit hardest, and who is already working on protection there.

/cooling-options/.text: What to build or change where people spend the hottest hours: homes, outdoor work, schools, markets and bus stops. For each option, what keeps it working, rough costs and the traps to avoid.

/corrections/.text: Every correction Common Shade has made, in the open: what was wrong, unclear or unfair, what changed and when. Part of how the site keeps its evidence honest.

/cotton-and-heat/.text: Heat reaches the people who grow, pick, move and process cotton in different ways. Follow the cotton from field to factory, see who carries the extra load, and which arrangements make protection usable.

/countries/.text: Snapshots of extreme heat in South and Southeast Asian countries: national plans and law, heat warnings, rules for heat at work, cooling, money for protection, and who is working on it.

/el-nino-and-cities/.text: What can smaller cities in India prepare before the next hot season? A practical guide to keeping protection working in workplaces, homes, schools and care services, and to the people, money and warnings needed to make it work.

/el-nino/.text: How El Niño in the Pacific can shift heat and rainfall across South and Southeast Asia, what the current official outlook says and what it cannot tell any one place, and what is worth preparing locally.

/evidence-map/.text: How sure are we about the cycles of extreme heat? Studies graded by kind, cycle by cycle, where the evidence looks stronger than the funding traced, and the questions nobody has answered yet.

/evidence/.text: What the evidence on extreme heat says, how sure we can be, and where every claim on Common Shade comes from: news, new research, the evidence map and the sources behind the site.

/factory-heat/.text: Heat inside factories depends on the building, machinery, humidity and the work itself. Explore how these conditions affect workers differently, which measures address them, and what makes protection practical on a real factory floor.

/factory-heat/worksheet/.text: A printable worksheet for worker representatives and managers to walk a factory floor together: record heat sources and what workers report, check whether people can use protection, and agree actions and how to know they worked.

/market-heat/.text: Heat in an open market depends on where people stand, what they carry and whether they can leave the stall. See who it reaches between dawn and dusk, which measures help vendors and porters drink, rest and keep earning, and what the evidence shows.

/cities/bengaluru/who-is-doing-what/.text: Who is working on heat in Bengaluru, and what are they actually doing? A new collective, ward climate plans, cooling centres and kits for outdoor workers, tools and announced money, with what is planned kept apart from what is delivered.

/cities/delhi/who-is-doing-what/.text: Who is working on heat in Delhi, and what is actually happening? The 2025 heat plan's promises beside what reporters found on the ground, vendor surveys, cool roof pilots and the research filling the gaps, each line checked against its source.

/cities/mumbai/who-is-doing-what/.text: Who is working on heat in Mumbai? A climate plan that names urban heat, a heat pathway for buildings written with C40, a stretched climate cell, and small efforts to cool homes in informal settlements, each checked against its source.

/cities/ahmedabad/who-is-doing-what/.text: Ahmedabad wrote South Asia's first city heat action plan. Who carries it now? Early warnings, cool roofs, a misted bus stop and heat insurance for women in informal work, with plans kept apart from delivery.

/cities/kolkata/who-is-doing-what/.text: Who is working on heat in Kolkata? Mapped heat zones, lost water bodies, a state heat wave plan and calls for a city plan: what the sources show, and what they do not, each line checked against its source.

/cities/chennai/who-is-doing-what/.text: Who is working on heat in Chennai? Cool roofs on schools with UNEP, a planned heat unit with CEEW, and heat mapping folded into the master plan, with planned kept apart from delivered and each line checked against its source.

/cities/hyderabad/who-is-doing-what/.text: How did a small cool roof pilot in Hyderabad become a state policy? The roof targets, the summer heat measures and who works on them, with plans kept apart from delivery and each line checked against its source.

/cities/bhubaneswar/who-is-doing-what/.text: Bhubaneswar links heat to cooling demand in a new integrated plan. Who wrote it, what it proposes for greening and buildings, and what is still only planned, each line checked against its source.

/cities/dhaka/who-is-doing-what/.text: Who is working on heat in Dhaka? Asia's first city Chief Heat Officer, a Red Crescent early action that released cash and cooling before the worst heat, and the data for a proposed city plan, each checked against its source.

/cities/kathmandu/who-is-doing-what/.text: Kathmandu set a heat record in 2024. Who is working on it? Studies, greening and calls for a plan, with an honest account of what the public sources show and what they do not.

/heat-tools/artpark_heat_forecast/.text: ARTPARK describes sub-district heat-risk forecasts for Karnataka up to seven days ahead, built with state agencies. See what is known about access, users and accuracy, and why a forecast horizon is not proof it works.

/heat-tools/cstep_deft/.text: A tool in development to judge where blue-green measures could cut heatwave and flood risk in Bengaluru. See what it is meant to produce, who it is for, and what is not yet public.

/heat-tools/heatwatch_apartment_charter/.text: A heat safety charter for the people who work in apartment complexes, from domestic staff to security guards and delivery workers, in English, Kannada and Hindi. See what it covers and what is not yet known.

/market-heat/worksheet/.text: A one-page heat check for vendor associations, women's collectives and market committees: walk the market together, note what people face and what stands in the way, check that no one loses a pitch, and agree three steps.

/finance/.text: How protection from extreme heat is paid for across Asia: who pays, how the money arrives, whether it lasts beyond one season, and what has been tried so far.

/for-ai/.text: Common Shade for AI assistants and the people who use them: a free, open evidence base on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia, with machine-readable files and every claim linked to its source.

/fund/.text: For funders and builders: where money for protection from extreme heat comes from, where it reaches, the businesses and ideas at work, and the questions worth asking before funding.

/glossary/.text: Plain-language explanations of the terms that come up again and again around extreme heat, from wet-bulb temperature to anticipatory action, each in a sentence or two.

/growing/.text: A public record of how Common Shade grows: each change, what it took to add, and how it connects to protection from extreme heat. Growth of the site, not protection achieved.

/guide/.text: How to use Common Shade: two questions to find your path, the four parts of the site, five tools that build on each other, and a running order for a 90-minute workshop.

/heat-assembly/.text: A shaded hall opens beside the market, and almost nobody who needs it can use it. Take a seat at the table, make agreements over four rounds of heat, and see who could take a break and why.

/heat-economy/businesses/.text: Businesses offering protection from extreme heat, from cool roofs and efficient fans to cold storage for medicine, with many working in South and Southeast Asia, and the questions to ask before buying.

/heat-economy/conditions/.text: Questions to ask before you buy, fund or start something that protects people from heat: does it work here, is it fair, who keeps it running, who pays, and who carries the risk?

/heat-economy/flows/.text: Follow the money for protection from extreme heat: traced funding from who gave it to the vicious cycles it could help break, and the cycles no traced funding has reached yet.

/heat-economy/.text: The businesses, funding and ideas that protect people from heat in Asia, how the heat economy works, and what to ask before you buy, fund or start something.

/heat-economy/money/careers/.text: Heat resilience needs people in health, engineering, labour rights, community organising, finance, research and policy. Roles connected to protection from extreme heat, each with its source and a clear note on whether it is still open.

/heat-economy/money/.text: Who funds protection from extreme heat and how each programme can be reached: the funding landscape, what still needs funding, open calls, careers, and the funding traced so far.

/heat-economy/money/opportunities/.text: Open calls and tenders connected to extreme heat: grants, prizes, technical assistance and procurement notices, each showing who can apply, when it closes and when its source was last checked.

/heat-economy/opportunities/.text: Ideas for businesses and services that protect people from extreme heat, one or more for each vicious cycle: who could pay, who it helps, and what needs to be in place first.

/heat-network/.text: Organisations across Asia and the world already working on parts of extreme heat, filterable by place, action and the part they play. Being listed describes published work, not partnership or endorsement.

/heat-tools/.text: Which heat tool fits your decision? Compare tools for heat warnings, risk assessment, cooling, protection planning and El Niño preparation in South and Southeast Asia: what each needs, what it gives and where its limits matter.

/heat-tools/asmc_enso/.text: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's reading of El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole, with typical regional effects. Its Heat Tool Finder profile explains that typical effects are past tendencies, not this season's forecast for any province.

/heat-tools/cs_enso_worksheet/.text: A one-page El Niño preparedness worksheet for a municipal team and a local organisation: agree what will be working before the hot season, and who keeps it working. It forecasts nothing; local warnings set the timing.

/heat-tools/wmo_gscu/.text: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update: multi-model probabilities for temperature and rainfall over the next three months, and the state of the main ocean drivers. Too coarse for a district, so read it with your national service.

/heatwaves/.text: Heatwaves that shaped South and Southeast Asia since 1998: what happened, what they cost and what changed afterwards. Recorded deaths are a floor, not a total, and the timeline says so where no solid count exists.

/how-heat-became-visible/.text: When did science, health, labour, finance and the UN begin to notice extreme heat, and who was still missing? A graded timeline of turning points, and how heat appears in IPCC reports.

/how-heat-is-reported/.text: How news reporting on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia follows protection, from a named responsibility through money and delivery to results: an explorer, worked examples and a kit for developing a reporting question.

/intersections/.text: Why does the same heatwave reach people so differently? Meet eight composite people on one street, share out a limited set of protections, and redesign them to see who protection reaches.

/join/.text: Help build Common Shade, a free and open evidence base on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia. Three ways in, whatever your work, and clear promises about what happens after you write.

/lancet-countdown-2026/.text: The 2026 Lancet Countdown read for extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia: the key numbers, what they mean for cities, health workers, employers, communities and funders, and what the evidence cannot show yet.

/live-through-a-heatwave/.text: Three ways to feel a heatwave from the inside: a worker's week, a hot night at home and a clinic visit, and a city's power, water and clinics under strain. Plus a table game for groups.

/loops/.text: The vicious cycles in which extreme heat feeds itself, traps people or overwhelms institutions: where each plays out in Asia, the evidence behind it, and the actions that could break it.

/news/.text: Recent headlines about extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia, alongside new research, refreshed automatically and linked to the original reporting.

/paths/.text: Short guided routes through Common Shade for funders, city teams, health workers, employers, community organisations, national governments and researchers. Pick your role and follow a handful of stops.

/paying-for-protection/.text: Protection from heat only works if someone pays for it, the money arrives in time, and it is still there next season. Start from what needs paying for, not from a financial product.

/paying-when-heat-strikes/.text: Which layer of money could carry extreme heat? Insurance, pools, credit, forecast-based funds and social protection in South and Southeast Asia: what exists, whether it paid out, and how quickly.

/plan/.text: Turn the map of extreme heat into a plan you can run: six steps to choose what to protect, who acts, what triggers action and how it is paid for. Your work stays in your browser.

/practical-actions/.text: Practical actions against extreme heat in workplaces, homes, schools, health facilities and markets, and what municipalities can do before summer. Each says who it protects, who acts, what it takes to run and what could stop it.

/practical/.text: Find practical actions against extreme heat by setting: what works, who does it, what keeps it working, and the evidence behind each one.

/print/.text: Printable one-page briefs on extreme heat for officials, planners, partners and journalists: practical actions by setting, city briefs, cooling options and short explainers. Free to print and share under CC BY 4.0.

/print/community-workshop-guide/.text: A printable plan for a 90-minute heat meeting in your community or workplace: start from what people know, follow one worker's week, find what you can do yourselves, and agree what to ask of partners.

/print/dry-and-humid-heat/.text: Dry heat and humid heat harm the body in different ways and need different warnings and cooling. A printable one-page explainer for anyone writing heat warnings, work rules or heat action plans.

/print/el-nino-briefing/.title: El Niño and heat in Asia: printable briefing
/print/el-nino-briefing/.text: A printable one-page briefing on El Niño and heat in Asia: what El Niño is, the current official outlook with its dates, what it cannot tell any one place, and a short checklist before the hot season.

/print/el-nino-worksheet/.text: A one-page worksheet for protecting one setting before the heat: choose the place, agree who runs it, set three pause points to tick on the day, and check what was missed. Filled in together at one meeting.

/print/four-heats/.text: A heat warning gives one number, but a family under a tin roof lives with four, and the worst often comes after dark. A printable one-page explainer with questions for heat action plans.

/print/heatwaves/.text: A printable one-page summary of the heatwaves that shaped South and Southeast Asia since 1998: what they cost, what changed afterwards, and four lessons for the next hot season.

/print/paying-for-protection/.text: A printable one-page guide to paying for heat protection: what needs paying for and when, the triggers that release money, why someone can lose income and get no payout, and whether it will last.

/print/weather-work-person/.text: The same thermometer reading can be safe for one person and dangerous for another. A printable one-page explainer on where weather, work and the person meet, with questions for heat action plans.

/print/workshop-guide/.text: A printable running order for a 90-minute workshop using Common Shade: a shared picture first, then one worker's week, then a plan with owners, money and triggers, and decisions recorded before people leave.

/privacy/.text: What Common Shade keeps, what it asks other services for, and the terms for reusing its text, data and films. Visitors' own inputs stay in their browser.

/resources/heat-action-plans/.text: Archives of heat action plans and related guidance from South and Southeast Asia, with a link to each original document, so planners, researchers and journalists can see what places have already written down.

/resources/heat-action-plans/india/.text: A searchable archive of Indian heat action plans, heat-health plans and guidance, with a link to each original document and how it was checked. A growing archive, not a complete collection.

/resources/.text: Archives and downloadable collections from Common Shade: heat action plans with links to the original documents, printable one-pagers for meetings and offices, and the sources behind every page of the site.

/shared-heat/.text: One market through one hot season: how a hot day ties lives together through shared places, work and services, why people sharing the heat do not share the same power over it, and what makes protection last.

/signals/all/.text: Every record on Common Shade's Signals on one page, newest first: commitments, findings, gatherings and guidance on extreme heat, each with what the evidence confirms so far.

/signals/.text: Which way is heat policy moving in South and Southeast Asia? Commitments, findings and guidance followed step by step, with what the evidence confirms for each promise and what would show the next step.

/social-protection/.text: Which public schemes could help a household through a hot season? Support across South and Southeast Asian countries, the steps people take to reach it, how it is delivered, and where no public system responds yet.

/solutions/.text: Ways to protect people from extreme heat, from shade and cool roofs to cooling, plans, rules and money that make protection last, each with its evidence, rough costs and what it depends on.

/sources/.text: Every source Common Shade cites, in one searchable list: research, reports, guidance, news and data, so any claim on the site can be traced back to where it came from.

/together/.text: Protection from extreme heat only reaches people when everyone it depends on plays their part. A coordinator's simulation: who has to say yes, and what happens when one does not?

/understand/.text: Start here to understand extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia: what it does, where, to whom, and how one harm leads to the next.

/use-with-ai/.text: Plain-text evidence packs on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia, one per country, vicious cycle and action, ready to load into the AI assistant or notebook tool you already use, with starter questions.

/whats-new/.text: State of the field: a monthly briefing on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia, built around one argument, with what moved, what it rests on, its sources and dates, and the questions still open.

/whats-new/2026-10/.text: State of the field, October 2026: support announced for the work between institutions, with amounts and delivery still to show. A monthly briefing on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia, with sources and dates.

/whats-new/2026-11/.text: State of the field, November 2026: a heat rule for outdoor work is scheduled to take effect, and whether rules reach workers is not yet visible. A monthly briefing on extreme heat in South and Southeast Asia.

/who-holds-it/.text: For protection from heat to reach people, someone has to permit it, pay for it, deliver it and check it. Choose an action to see the kinds of body involved and the organisations already at work.

/who-is-at-risk/.text: The same heatwave lands differently. Who extreme heat hits hardest depends on how exposed people are and what stands between them and safety, from farming households to outdoor workers and pregnant women.

/worked-plans/.text: How places in Asia have turned heat risk into a plan, from Ahmedabad and Thane to Tamil Nadu, Singapore and Dhaka: what happened, what they decided, what changed, and who leads each action.
